key_insight: VR-Adam-SHANG combines variance reduction, adaptive preconditioning, and acceleration to achieve expected objective-gap bounds with O(1/K²) initial-energy decay plus an O(1/√K) stochastic term.
engineering_relevance: The methods offer accelerated stochastic convex optimization with at most two sampled-gradient evaluations per iteration and no full-gradient refreshes.
method: Use STORM-type recursive estimation to reduce gradient noise.
Combine scalar or diagonal Adam-style preconditioning with SHANG acceleration and correction.
Apply prescribed initialization and polynomial step schedules to obtain O(1/K) mean-square gradient-estimation error.
evidence_signal: At matched sample-gradient budgets, at least one of the two variants achieved the lowest mean terminal objective gap among compared methods in every tested setting.
watch_item: The guarantees assume smooth convex objectives, unbiased sampling, bounded variance, and mean-square smoothness of gradient noise; they do not establish performance for general nonconvex problems.
paper_title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning
